title: Ndomba Oka (Fish Steamed in Banana Leaf)
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik.com)
desc: Fresh fish marinated 15 minutes with green condiments, onion, chilli and garlic, wrapped in wilted banana leaves over odzom leaves, boiled about 1 hour on a plate, then finished 30 minutes on embers.
longDesc: A fish parcel from Afrik. The fish is cleaned and cut; green condiments and onions are chopped over it; chilli, garlic and white pepper are crushed with a little water and added; salt, and marinate about 15 minutes. The banana leaves are passed over a flame and the rib removed. Odzom leaves go on the leaf, then the fish, tied. The parcel sits on a plate in a pot with a little water so it does not sit in the water, closed and boiled about 1 hour, then finished on barbecue embers about 30 minutes ‘so the remaining water evaporates’. Served hot.
ingredients: Onions — in the method, not in the list
Salt and white pepper — quantities not printed
steps: Clean and cut the fish. Chop the green condiments and onions over the fish.
Crush the chilli, garlic and white pepper with a little water. Add them with salt and marinate about 15 minutes.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame and remove the central rib.
Lay the odzom leaves on a leaf, then the fish, and tie the parcel.
Stand the parcel on a plate in a pot with a little water, so it is not in the water. Close and boil about 1 hour.
Finish on barbecue embers about 30 minutes so the remaining water evaporates. Serve hot.
chefTips: The only printed cue is the parcel’s smell: the odzom has ‘une odeur toute particulière’.
Keep the parcel on a plate so it steams above the water.
Quantities for several condiments are not printed — season by taste.
commonMistakes: Letting the parcel sit in the water.
Not removing the leaf rib, which can tear the parcel.
healthBenefits: Fish steamed in leaves adds protein with little added fat.
culturalNote: The page names no community. Other sources attribute ndomba to Bantu and forest peoples, but those pages were unattributed and are not used.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Ndomba oka’. Byline as printed: ‘Amina Savoura’. ‘Publié le 30 mai 2011 à 18h56’. Serves 5. TWO-PASS.
ABSENT, not estimated: quantities for ossim nnam, messep, garlic, chilli and onions; the amount of water in the pot.
